newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end lower, tracking Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end lower, tracking Wall Street.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed softer with electricity stocks among the steepest decliners, said traders.
The bolsa is expected to decline again at the opening as investors take profits after the mini-rally at the start of the week, they said.
"We see the market ending the week flat with stocks ticking lower over the next couple of days," said Guillermo Tagle, director of research at Santander Investment.
The selective IPSA index ended unofficially off 0.88 percent at 90.85 points.
The general IGPA index lost 0.48 percent to 4,995.27 points.
Turnover was light with volume of 8.8 billion pesos.
The bolsa was undermined by sharp falls in Chilean-issued American Depositary Receipts which tumbled on the slump in the Dow Jones index, said dealers.
"If Wall Street rises, Chile is 100 percent independent. But as soon as Wall Street falls, Chile becomes 100 percent dependent," said one trader.
Electricity stocks closed with steep falls in Santiago and New York on fears over the impact of lower prices and this year's drought on companies' earnings, said brokers.
Enersis shed 1.32 percent to 224 pesos with Endesa off 1.11 percent to 222-1/2 pesos.
Winners included copper products maker Madeco, up 1.02 percent at 990 pesos, power utility Chilectra, up 0.45 percent at 2,240 pesos and brewery CCU which gained 0.33 percent to 1,500 pesos.
